verdict.line: You can lose extended trades in the first two levels when Tahm's Q poke and Thick Skin sustain outvalue you, but from level 3 on you win almost every all-in once your passive and Death's Grasp combo are online.

brief.thesis: Tahm Kench is built to win the opening levels — his Q (Tongue Lash) pokes and heals him while his E (Thick Skin) banks damage into free sustain, and OP.GG's own read is that he is at his strongest before level 3. Mordekaiser's whole kit — Darkness Rise stacking, Obliterate's single-target bonus, Death's Grasp's pull — only comes together once he has his full four abilities, at which point the trade math flips hard in his favor. That split explains the 56.6% win rate over 302 games with both lane and solo-kill advantage: this is a lane you survive early and then dominate.

theirWindow.when: Levels 1-2, before your kit is online
theirWindow.what: Tahm's Q (Tongue Lash) slows and heals him on hit while stacking An Acquired Taste, and his E (Thick Skin) is quietly banking every point of damage you land into a free heal. Farm from max range, don't trade autos into his poke, and don't let him sit on 3 stacks near his Q range of 900.

yourWindow.when: From level 3, after proc'ing Darkness Rise
yourWindow.what: Once you've landed three attacks or spells on him your passive Darkness Rise lights up — damage aura plus move speed. Use E (Death's Grasp) to pull him in if he tries to walk off, then Q (Obliterate) for its bonus single-target damage and finish the all-in under the aura.

start.item: Doran's Ring + Health Potion + Health Potion
start.why: The double potion covers the HP you lose to Tahm's early Q poke while you wait out his level 1-2 window, and Doran's Ring's mana keeps you spamming Obliterate on minions to stay even on gold.

boots.why: Tahm's whole damage profile — Q, R (Devour), his passive bonus damage — is magic, and the tenacity shortens how long his Q slow and the stun from stacked Acquired Taste lock you down.

core.why: The slow on every ability lets you stick Obliterate and Death's Grasp on Tahm through his Abyssal Dive, turning your all-in windows into guaranteed trades.
Omnivamp matches his Thick Skin sustain war and the true-damage proc rewards exactly the extended melee trades this lane turns into after level 6.
The burn punishes Tahm's high total health, which is also what scales his own passive damage against you, so it directly answers his power source.

situational.when: the game runs long and you need your W (Indestructible) heal and Riftmaker omnivamp amplified for extended skirmishes
tahm is leaning hard on his thick skin and devour self-healing and you need grievous wounds to cut it
you need the extra ability haste to loop obliterate and death's grasp faster in a grindy stalemate

runes.keystoneWhy: This lane is a long trade war, not a burst duel — Conqueror's stacking adaptive force and healing on takedown rewards the exact extended melee exchanges you're forcing once your kit is online.

summoners.why: You already hold lane and solo-kill advantage on paper — Ignite converts your level 3+ all-ins into kills by cutting through Tahm's Thick Skin and Devour sustain, and it's the highest-picked (78.8%) and best-performing (55.4%) combo in the data.

playing.title: Farm safe before level 3
playing.detail: Tahm's Q (Tongue Lash) poke plus the free healing from Thick Skin wins trades outright at levels 1-2. Last-hit from max range and decline extended autoattack exchanges until you have your full combo.

playing.title: Track Acquired Taste stacks
playing.detail: Every Q hit stacks An Acquired Taste on you; at 3 stacks his next Q stuns and consumes them. Don't stand in his 900-range Q window once you're near that third stack.

playing.title: All-in only after passive procs
playing.detail: Darkness Rise needs 3 landed attacks or spells on him first. Open with E (Death's Grasp) to pull him in if he tries to disengage, then Obliterate for its single-target bonus once the aura is live.

playing.title: Pre-bank your shield
playing.detail: W (Indestructible) stores damage dealt and taken before you can consume it for the heal — pop it before the trade starts so it's already banking value when his Q and autos land.

playing.title: Trade when Abyssal Dive is down
playing.detail: His W is a 21-17s cooldown dash that's both his engage and his only escape. When it's on cooldown he can't reposition or flee, so that's when you extend fights.

playing.title: Ult to remove him from fights
playing.detail: R (Realm of Death) drags him into your dimension and steals his stats — use it to isolate him from a dangerous skirmish, and if you kill him you keep the stolen stats until he respawns.

playing.title: Build into his sustain
playing.detail: Rylai's into Riftmaker and Liandry's gives you the slow to stick on him plus the burn and omnivamp to outlast his Thick Skin and Devour healing over a long game.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, runes, summoners, and all win-rate figures above are measured from actual games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning — why the early game is his and the mid-to-late game is yours — is my own tactical read, not sourced data.

stats.opponentTip: Tahm Kench is extremely strong before he reaches level 3. Focus on farming lane and afterwards use [P] to fight him after leveling up.
